clue.text: It's shown in clever caption

indicators.note: being shown in something means sitting inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: clever means subtle
the word it, with the 's (is) acting as a link

explanation.surface: A witty caption appears under a cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtitles are the printed captions shown beneath film footage.

clue.text: Inauguration of school to develop charm

indicators.note: an inauguration is a beginning, so the first letter of school is taken

parts.note: to educe is to draw out or develop

explanation.surface: Opening a school to cultivate charm.
explanation.definitionFit: To seduce is to win over by allure, a verb sense of charm.

clue.text: Minstrel boy infiltrates a rebel organisation

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside the group
organisation means arrangement, so the letters are put into order anew

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A singer's son infiltrates a rebel group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges A REBEL to BALEER, and LAD goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A minstrel was a singer of ballads.

clue.text: Patient finds it's having no effect

explanation.surface: A patient learns the treatment is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick or disabled person needing care is an invalid (stressed on the first syllable); void or null is invalid (stressed on the second).

clue.text: It's ghastly being in Honolulu? Ridiculous!

indicators.note: being in shows the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs that Honolulu is horrid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shocking or gruesome.

clue.text: King Henry. Transylvania's first monarch to swing, perhaps

parts.note: R (rex) is the abbreviation for king
Hy is an old written abbreviation of the name Henry

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word Transylvania's

parts.note: HM stands for His or Her Majesty, a monarch

explanation.surface: A King Henry and the first ruler of Transylvania dance to swing music.
explanation.walkthrough: HM (His/Her Majesty) and R (Rex) are standard crossword monarchs; Hy for Henry is rarer.
explanation.definitionFit: Swing is one example of a musical beat or pulse, a type of regular beat.

clue.text: Toffee-nosed topper

explanation.surface: A snooty top hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee-nosed is British slang for snobbish, which is high-hat; a topper is a tall hat.

clue.text: The charge to trap river fish

indicators.note: to trap means to enclose the river letter inside

parts.note: a toll is a charge for passage

explanation.surface: A fee is paid to snare fish in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat.

clue.text: Wet blankets fail to hold water

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the water goes within

parts.note: to miss is to fail
Erie is a North American lake, a body of water

explanation.surface: Damp bedding cannot keep water in.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy killjoys are called misery-guts or wet blankets.

clue.text: Bird painter

explanation.surface: A bird artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistlers are a family of Australasian songbirds; James McNeill Whistler was an American painter.

clue.text: So delighted over resolution to honour an agreement

indicators.note: a resolution is a working-out or re-sorting, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at a resolution passed to keep a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' rearranges the fifteen letters of SO DELIGHTED OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up with what was promised is the idiom for fulfilling a bargain.

clue.text: After a stroke the journalist was slow-moving

indicators.note: after places the journalist's letters behind the stroke's

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke
ED, the editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist moved sluggishly after suffering a stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep along is to move very slowly, past tense matching.

clue.text: Don finds it's sunny outside church

indicators.note: outside means the sunny word goes around the church abbreviation

parts.note: solar means of the sun, hence sunny

explanation.surface: A university lecturer discovers it is bright outside the chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university academic, a learned person.

clue.text: Abrupt stumble into a trap

parts.note: dead can mean sudden or abrupt, as in a dead stop
to stumble is to fall

explanation.surface: Someone trips suddenly and lands in a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadfall is a hunting snare in which a heavy weight drops onto the prey.

clue.text: Rising confusion in island rally

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards
in puts the confusion inside the island

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
a mess is confusion

explanation.surface: Chaos rises at an island gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reads the whole assembly upwards, as suits a down light; 'in' sets the confusion within the island.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally troops is to gather them together.

clue.text: Experience a smack

explanation.surface: Someone tries out being slapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To experience something is to get a sample of it; a smack is a slight flavour, as in a smack of garlic.

clue.text: Game played in a ring?

parts.note: a one-player card game shares its name with a single gemstone set in a ring

explanation.surface: A game played in a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire is both a game for one and a single gem mounted in a ring.

clue.text: Ship's chandler, perhaps, required for repairs after docking?

definitions.text: Ship's chandler, perhaps, required for repairs after docking?

parts.words: Ship's chandler, perhaps, required for repairs after docking?
parts.note: a chandler sells goods to ships, but docking also means cutting off a tail, so someone who puts tails back is jokingly suggested

explanation.surface: A ship's supplier is needed for repairs once a vessel docks.
explanation.walkthrough: Docking also means cutting off an animal's tail; read as RE-TAILER, someone who restores tails.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's chandler is a shopkeeper, one who sells goods to the public.

clue.text: Set in clay

explanation.surface: Something fixed into wet clay.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a badger's burrow, like a fox's den; clay is a kind of soil.

clue.text: Many a vandal reported in alarm

parts.note: the Huns, like the Vandals, were barbarian invaders

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so the word is used for its sound

parts.note: dread is alarm or fear

explanation.surface: Many vandals were described as alarming.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred is a large number, so it can stand for many.

clue.text: Girl leaving area likely to be evacuated? Exactly!

indicators.note: the girl leaving the area means her letters are removed from it

parts.note: a district is an area
Di is a short girl's name

indicators.note: evacuating a word empties out its middle, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A girl leaves a district that is probably going to be cleared, absolutely.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing DI from DISTRICT gives STRICT; LIKELY emptied leaves LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Strictly and precisely both mean in an exact manner.

clue.text: An itch one develops to get a drink

indicators.note: develops means grows into something else, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An itch someone develops leads them to a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develops' rearranges AN ITCH to CHIANT; the I for 'one' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red Italian wine.

clue.text: Born truly talented

parts.note: right can mean truly, as in right royal

explanation.surface: Someone born with true talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever, gifted person is called bright.

clue.text: A familiar starter for menus in the NAAFI, for instance

parts.note: a familiar is a close friend, a crony

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so the first letter of menus is taken

explanation.surface: A close friend chooses a first course from the forces canteen menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAAFI (Navy, Army and Air Force Institutes) runs British forces canteens, so its menus suit the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: NAAFI is a word formed from initial letters, an example of that type of abbreviation.

clue.text: Fees for judges

explanation.surface: Charges set for the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Rates are charges or fees; rates is also a verb meaning assesses or judges.

clue.text: Flyer cut short enthusiastic attack, initially gaining height

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: avid means enthusiastic

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of attack

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, a height

explanation.surface: A pilot curtails a keen assault after first climbing higher.
explanation.walkthrough: AVID cut short gives AVI; 'gaining' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot of an aircraft is a flyer.

clue.text: Pledge announced to support bill for a special purpose

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath

parts.note: an ad is a bill or poster

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the word is used for its sound

parts.note: to hock is to pawn or pledge

explanation.surface: A promise is announced to back legislation intended for one purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Ad hoc is Latin for 'for this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc describes something set up for one particular job.

clue.text: Talking Latin with her makes a good approach to clue solving

definitions.text: a good approach to clue solving

indicators.note: makes signals that these letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Chatting with her in Latin is a fine way to crack crossword clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges TALKING LATIN plus HER; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking creatively and indirectly is just what cryptic clues demand.

clue.text: Live broadcast is relayed without music

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order
without means the music's letters are left out

parts.note: relayed on air means re-aired
an air is a tune, music

explanation.surface: A live broadcast is repeated with the music cut.
explanation.walkthrough: REAIRED less AIR leaves RED; 'broadcast' then rearranges IS plus RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To live somewhere is to dwell there.

clue.text: I would stress — outside chance

indicators.note: outside means the stress word wraps around the I would letters

parts.note: an accent is a stress on a syllable
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: Someone insists that something lies beyond probability.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is something happening by luck rather than design.
